newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY PUTS INDIA IN DRIVING SEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY PUTS INDIA IN DRIVING SEAT.

text.p: A chanceless century by opener Navjot Sidhu and contrasting fifties by Rahul Dravid and Sachin Tendulkar left India in command on 280 for three at the close of the first day of the first test against Sri Lanka on Saturday.
Sidhu's impressive 111 in 260 minutes on a slow, deadpan wicket was his eighth in tests and his third against Sri Lanka.
Dravid's ninth test half century was a painstaking effort. He took 252 minutes over his 69, hitting 10 fours.
By comparison his skipper Tendulkar was in scintillating form . He took 19 off one Chaminda Vaas over and reached his 19th test 50 in just 89 minutes.
The second new ball proved especially expensive for the Sri Lankans with Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin plundering 31 off five overs.
Sri Lanka's only success during the opening two sessions came when Nayan Mongia was caught at third slip by debutant Mahela Jayawardena for seven.
Sidhu and Dravid then shared a 147-run second partnership, ended when Sidhu attempted a cover drive off Vass. The ball took an outside edge and flew straight to wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana.
Sidhu's 111 included two sixes and 13 fours.
Dravid fell in unfortunate circumstances. His drive rebounded off the body of Marvan Atapattu at silly point and bowler Sanath Jayasuriya took a tumbling catch.
Tendulkar (65) and Azharuddin (18) then ended the day in a blaze of strokeplay, sharing a half century stand.
